chapter: Charlie Johnson, Willie Gant and the late 1920s
title: Water in the baritone and the Small's personnel
summary: A prank in which water was put in a baritone saxophone, and a list of the band members.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Skerritt Freddie Scarett, that's the man that was talking to me about seeing --

And Scarett and some baritone, guy used to play baritone (unintelligible) on our lunch hour, on intermission, and he all of a sudden just get high all the time, you know, big fellow, played baritone and alto. So when he come back to play the baritone, a lot of go way up and down like a fountain, everybody in the band sitting down and sitting in the cabaret, started laughing, say, how'd the water come from?

(unintelligible) the baritone. 'Who the hell put the water in the baritone,' he said. Man, you done drink so much, just spit in it. That's spit coming out. He said, that ain't no spit; somebody put water in it. The guys had put water in the baritone. See, because they got that three-note (unintelligible), and the water was (unintelligible) up in the air. Rex Jones on trumpet. Kenneth Kalton was on trumpet.

Kenneth Kalton. He was a head (unintelligible), and they had -- by the name of Joe Williams on trombone, and we had -- Willie was on the piano. We had -- Billy Taylor was on bass. He worked with Duke --
